instructions:
Trump Files original description-context rescue

Work only records in this input. This is offline proposal work: never edit canonical/live data or write Neon. Preserve supplied text, facts, exact URLs, IDs (including expanded IDs), and provenance. Inspect the staged row, frozen original when present, exact blocker, held204 terminal result when present, and supplied source URLs before deciding whether one focused rescue can resolve the gap. Do not add unrelated events, unsupported scoring, invented detail, filler, or broad research. At most ONE focused context rescue per record.

Return one append-only result per input record with the exact record_id and a terminal outcome: pass, hold, or exclusion_candidate. If pass, provide source-grounded reader-facing title, short, medium, and long descriptions; preserve adequate existing text. Limits: title <=180 characters; short <=180 characters; medium 45-90 words; long 140-300 words. No truncation or padding. Map each consulted URL to the facts it supports. A hold must state the precise remaining evidentiary/context gap. exclusion_candidate must explain why the record is not a discrete supported Trump event/action; it is a proposal only. Never turn a prior held204 release-ready flag into approval.

Suggested terminal JSON fields: record_id, outcome, proposed_title, proposed_description_short, proposed_description_medium, proposed_description_long, focused_rescue, sources_consulted (URL plus supported facts/limitations), remaining_gap, exclusion_reason, provenance. Keep output append-only and preserve input/history.

exact_blocker: needs_context: the official list confirms the offense label, sentence and pardon date but does not describe the robbery, identify the victim or explain the clemency decision. A case record or sourced account of the pardon is needed for a useful long explanation.

The DOJ list supports Floyd’s January 19, 2021 pardon, 2008 bank-robbery-by-extortion conviction, and listed sentence. It does not describe the robbery, identify the victim, or explain the clemency rationale or consequences. Still needed: a case record or sourced pardon account for a useful long description; the official index alone does not supply that narrative.

Focused direct read of the DOJ Office of the Pardon Attorney list returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-02. Its January 19, 2021 clemency section lists Steven Benjamin Floyd in the Southern District of Mississippi, convicted of bank robbery by extortion, and records a sentence imposed January 3, 2008: 30 months (the last six in a halfway house), three years’ supervised release, and a $2,500 fine. The linked DOJ clemency-record PDF returned HTTP 200 (283,926 bytes) but contains no extractable text in this read, so it added no narrative facts. The official list does not describe the robbery, identify a victim, or give the clemency rationale or consequences. Still missing for a useful long description: a case record or accessible sourced pardon account with those details; do not infer motive from the grant alone.
